dedupe_keys.name: detection of network disruptions at colocation facilities and ixps from traceroute data milolidakis fontugne and dimitropoulos

description: This paper devises a method to identify colocation facilities in traceroute data and to monitor delay and routing patterns between facilities, plus an anomaly detection technique that reports abnormal traffic changes usually caused by facility outages. It evaluates the method with eight months of traceroute data from the RIPE Atlas measurement platform and inspects the most prominent events by hand: an IXP outage, a DDoS attack and a power failure in a facility. It also examines the impact of anomalies at the metropolitan level and finds outages that span up to eight facilities. Producer: Alexandros Milolidakis, Romain Fontugne and Xenofontas Dimitropoulos, funded by an ERC grant, posted 12 November 2019. Coverage: worldwide facilities visible in RIPE Atlas traceroutes. Access: paper on arXiv; no code or event list link was read on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: detection depends on traceroute coverage and facility mapping, and only the abstract page was read. Simulation uses: the detected events and method support resilience studies of exchange points and data-centre facilities and validation of outage models. Related record: the CAIDA PeeringDB archive (data-caida-peeringdb-historical-archive), which supplies facility and IXP membership data.
